question: What prompts, practices, and patterns — from technical writing, editing, documentation, design-doc/RFC/PRD culture, and human–AI co-writing — would make an AI-assisted document co-authoring process produce better docs, and how should such docs be validated before shipping?

initial_facets.question: How should good technical/business docs be written: audience and purpose framing, BLUF / pyramid principle / inverted pyramid, concision and plain-language guidance, and revision/editing passes?
What do doc-type-specific templates and cultures (design doc, RFC, PRD, ADR, postmortem, decision memo, Amazon 6-pager/PR-FAQ, Diataxis) prescribe, and what makes them work?

How should docs be validated before shipping: reader testing/cold reads, comprehension checks, explain-it-back, review checklists, pre-mortem/red-team, claim verification, consistency checks, readability metrics and their limits, stakeholder review?

What does human-AI co-writing research and practitioner guidance (2023-2026) show about failure modes (homogenization, voice loss, verbosity, filler, hallucination, sycophancy) and effective interaction patterns?

What current LLM/agent prompting guidance (Anthropic, OpenAI, practitioners) is relevant to running a co-authoring workflow in Claude Code: subagents for fresh-eyes review, LLM-as-judge biases, avoiding over-structured output, skill authoring?

What comparable skills, tools, prompts and style guides exist for AI-assisted doc writing and review (agent skills repos, prose linters, Google/Microsoft style guides), and what do they do that upstream doc-coauthoring does not?
What observable markers of AI-generated prose ('slop') are documented, and how can a workflow detect and remove them?
